historical_references.reference: The title 'Rahmatul Lil-Alamin' was given to Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) by Allah in Surah Al-Rahman (55:1-6) of the Quran. The chapter is named after this title and is among the earliest chapters revealed to the Prophet. This title signifies that Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) is a source of mercy for all mankind and the best of creation.

The title 'Rahmatul Lil-Alamin' was also used by Prophet Ibrahim (AS) in his prayer for his son Ismail in Surah Al-Saffat (37:104) of the Quran. It indicates that Allah is the source of mercy for all mankind, including Ibrahim and Ismail, and that He is merciful towards all of His creation.

modern_usage.modern_context: The Islamic name 'Rahmath' which translates to 'mercy' or 'compassion' is increasingly being used in modern contexts, especially in discussions around leadership, women empowerment, and mental health awareness. Rahmath as a concept of mercy and compassion is now being applied to leadership styles, with many leaders adopting Rahmathic leadership that focuses on empathy, kindness, and understanding towards their teams. Rahmath is also being used as a call to action for women empowerment, with many using the term to describe a compassionate and inclusive society where women are valued and supported. Lastly, Rahmath is being recognized as a crucial aspect of mental health awareness and self-care, with many using the term to describe acts of self-compassion and kindness towards oneself.
